rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child's volunteering provision. Its rules cover registrants aged eighteen to twenty-six volunteering through their local boards, prompt classification, physical examination, and selection for induction. The child closely adapts that machinery for Class I-O registrants volunteering for civilian work and expressly directs that they be processed in the same manner as volunteers for induction, except that civilian work replaces induction. C22 is also materially related because it established the Class I-O and I-W classifications and their defining civilian-work language, but it is more a substantive regulatory foundation than the closest drafting template. C12 supplies earlier classification and conscientious-objector machinery but is less directly parallel.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any registrant who is between the ages of 18 and 26 and who has been classified in Class I-O, or who claims eligibility for classification in Class I-O, may volunteer at his local board for civilian work
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Registrants who have reached the eighteenth anniversary of the day of their birth and who have not reached the twenty-sixth anniversary of the day of their birth may volunteer at their local board for induction
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the same age limits, volunteer status, and local-board mechanism to civilian work.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The local board shall promptly classify any such volunteer who claims eligibility for Class I-O.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: When a man files an Application for Voluntary Induction... he shall be classified as soon as possible
shared_material.explanation: Both establish expedited classification specifically for volunteers.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Each such volunteer who is in Class I-O and who has been found acceptable for service after his armed forces physical examination shall be processed in the same manner as a volunteer for induction except that, in lieu of induction, he shall be ordered by the local board to perform civilian work
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A volunteer who is placed in Class I-A or Class I-A-O shall be selected for armed forces physical examination and for induction in the manner prescribed in Parts 1628 and 1631
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly borrows the volunteer-for-induction processing sequence and substitutes civilian-work assignment for induction.

shared_material.child_excerpt: registrants who have been classified in Class I-O... civilian work contributing to the maintenance of the national health, safety, or interest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Class I-O: Conscientious objector available for civilian work contributing to the maintenance of the national health, safety, or interest... Class I-W: Conscientious objector performing civilian work contributing to the maintenance of the national health, safety, or interest.
shared_material.explanation: C22 supplies the exact classification categories and defining phrase that the child operationalizes.
